```mjs
// Shared Stryker mutation-testing config for the Medusa monorepo.
//
// Usage: run from INSIDE the package you want to mutate, so Stryker picks up
// that package's own jest.config.js (each package has its own moduleNameMapper
// and transform settings), pointing at this shared file:
//
//   cd packages/modules/api-key
//   yarn stryker run ../../../stryker.config.mjs
//
// Narrow the scope with --mutate for faster runs, e.g.:
//   yarn stryker run ../../../stryker.config.mjs --mutate "src/services/**/*.ts"
//
// Do not run this from the repo root: the root jest.config.js fans out to
// every package as a multi-project config, which would mean mutating (and
// re-testing) the entire monorepo.

/** @type {import("@stryker-mutator/api/core").PartialStrykerOptions} */
export default {
  testRunner: "jest",

  jest: {
    // Use the jest.config.js found in the current working directory (the package).
    configFile: "jest.config.js",
    // Stryker's default injects its own config; keeping this enabled lets it
    // wrap the package config and run tests per mutant.
    enableFindRelatedTests: true,
  },

  // Only mutate source code; skip tests, type declarations, and barrel files.
  mutate: [
    "src/**/*.ts",
    "!src/**/__tests__/**",
    "!src/**/__mocks__/**",
    "!src/**/*.spec.ts",
    "!src/**/*.test.ts",
    "!src/**/*.d.ts",
    "!src/**/index.ts",
    "!src/migrations/**",
  ],

  // "perTest" coverage runs only the tests that touch each mutant, which is a
  // large speedup. Jest supports it natively.
  coverageAnalysis: "perTest",

  reporters: ["clear-text", "progress", "html"],
  htmlReporter: { fileName: "reports/mutation/index.html" },

  // Scratch dir for sandboxed copies of the code; ignored by git.
  tempDirName: ".stryker-tmp",

  // Thresholds are informational for now (break: null never fails the run).
  thresholds: { high: 80, low: 60, break: null },

  // Mutation runs are CPU heavy; keep parallelism modest on laptops.
  concurrency: 2,
  timeoutMS: 60000,
}

```

D6 - Mutation Testing (new)¶
This is a new individual deliverable.

What it is. A mutation testing tool makes small changes to your code (mutants), such as flipping a condition or changing a boundary value, and runs your tests against each one. If a test fails, the mutant is killed. If all tests pass, the mutant survived: your tests did not notice that the code changed. Survivors point to weak or missing tests.

What to do. For one of your issues whose PR changes source code and tests (CSCI 535: two such issues; your small issue may be one of them):

Run a mutation testing tool on the source files changed by your PR(s) for that issue. Do not run it on the whole project.
Using the tool's report, analyze every surviving mutant: is it equivalent (it behaves exactly like the original code, so no test can kill it), or does it reveal a gap in your tests? If there are more than 10 surviving mutants, analyze at least 10, starting with those in lines your PR added or changed.
Add or strengthen at least one test that kills a surviving mutant that revealed a gap. Re-run the tool to confirm it is killed. If no surviving mutant reveals a gap (all are killed or equivalent), say so and justify it in the surviving-mutants table; that completes this step.
Answer the questions in the template below.
Evidence. Configure the tool to write a machine-readable report (StrykerJS: add "json" to reporters; Gremlins: --output=<file>.json; go-mutesting: save the terminal output to a text file). Commit the report from your first run and from your re-run as docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json and -after.json (.txt for go-mutesting). The mutation scores you list must match the reports, and the mutant your new test kills must show as killed in the "after" report.

A tool is required. Manual mutation does not count.

Stack    Tool
TypeScript/JavaScript with Vitest (Actual Budget, Cal.diy, Excalidraw, Outline, Gitea frontend)    StrykerJS with the Vitest runner
TypeScript/JavaScript with Jest (Medusa)    StrykerJS with the Jest runner
Go (Gitea backend)    Gremlins or go-mutesting
Set it up early. Getting the tool to work on a large codebase is real work: builds, services, and choosing which tests run. Each student configures and runs the tool for their own files and commits the configuration they used. You may reuse a teammate's setup (and are encouraged to), as long as you run the tool yourself and credit the teammate in your report.

Common problems to watch for:

The tool stops before mutating. Tools first run your tests on the unchanged code. If any of the selected tests fail, the run stops. Fix or exclude failing tests first (this is where your baseline run helps).
Tests run against built code. If your tests run against compiled output (for example, a dist folder) instead of the source, mutants in the source are never seen by the tests. Configure the tool to rebuild before testing, or choose tests that run on source.
Tests need services. Some test suites need a database or another service running. Start them before running the tool.
False survivors. If you limit which tests run (for example, with Vitest's dir option), make sure the tests that cover the mutated files are included. Otherwise, mutants that some test would catch are reported as survived or not covered. Before writing a new test for a survivor, check that the relevant tests actually ran.
Long runs. Mutating only the files changed by your PR keeps run time manageable.

If your chosen issue touches both, the rubric says to run the tool on the source files the PR changed. You could do two runs, or pick the issue whose changes are mostly in one stack.

Unit specs, such as your dashboard `.spec.tsx` or any mocked service tests, are much cheaper. That may influence which files give you the best mutation analysis.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5-5 2026-11-18 03:50:32Z)**_

Yes, it should work, as long as the baseline run is green. Pick one or two source files rather than your whole PR. I haven't looked at your actual changes, so this is based on the file layout in your git status.

**Why one or two files is enough:**
- The rubric says to run on "the source files changed by your PR", but it also needs you to analyze every survivor, or at least 10 if there are more. A single file with real logic often produces 10 to 40 mutants. Several files can produce hundreds of survivors you'd have to triage.
- Run time scales with mutants times test time. One file keeps each iteration to minutes, and you run twice (before and after).
- The one file should contain actual logic: branches, comparisons, string and array handling. Mutation testing finds little in pure wiring, types, or barrel files.

**Candidates from your git status, best first:**
- **`product-activity-actor.ts`:** a small util. It probably has conditionals that decide the actor, which makes it a good source of meaningful mutants.
- **The subscriber** (`subscribers/product-activity.ts`): probably worth it if it has logic you unit test with mocks.
- **The module service in `packages/modules/product-activity`:** skip it if it mostly extends `MedusaService`, because there's little hand-written logic. Also skip it if its tests are DB integration tests.

**Things to check before committing to a file:**
1. **The test runs against source, not `dist`.** The Jest config uses `@swc/jest` on `src`, which is fine.
2. **The unit tests for that file are in the same package and need no DB.** If a spec imports the module service with a real database, it's an integration test and will be slow or fail.
3. **The baseline passes.** In your main checkout, run the package's Jest tests once first. Stryker aborts if any test fails on unmutated code.
4. **Your Finder duplicates** (`... 2.ts`, `... 3.ts`) are out of the way. They could match Stryker's glob, and a duplicate spec and source pair would skew results.

**One caveat on scope.** If one file gives fewer than ~10 mutants, or all of them are killed, that's still acceptable under the rubric. You'd justify it in the table. Still, a file with a few more branches gives you a more interesting analysis, so I'd start with the actor util plus the subscriber if both have unit tests.

If you tell me which files have specs, I can check each file for logic density and whether its specs run standalone, then suggest the exact `--mutate` target.

```text
42	  after: Record<string, unknown>
43	): ProductActivityChange[] {
44	  const changes: ProductActivityChange[] = []
45	  const keys = new Set([...Object.keys(before), ...Object.keys(after)])
46	
47	  for (const field of keys) {
48	    const from = before[field] ?? null
49	    const to = after[field] ?? null
50	    if (stable(from) !== stable(to)) {
51	      changes.push({ field, from, to })
52	    }
53	  }
54	
55	  return changes
56	}
57	
58	/**
59	 * Compares two snapshots of the same product and returns one draft per
60	 * difference: the product's own fields, then each variant, option, image and
61	 * relation that was added, removed or changed.
62	 */
63	export function diffSnapshots(
64	  prev: ProductSnapshot,
65	  next: ProductSnapshot,
66	  productId: string
67	): ActivityDraft[] {
68	  const drafts: ActivityDraft[] = []
69	
70	  const productChanges = diffFields(prev.product.fields, next.product.fields)
71	  if (productChanges.length) {
72	    drafts.push({
73	      action: "updated",
74	      entity_type: "product",
75	      entity_id: productId,
76	      entity_label: next.product.label,
77	      changes: productChanges,
78	    })
79	  }
80	
81	  for (const { type, attach } of CHILD_ENTITY_TYPES) {
82	    // Old snapshots may predate a type added later, so default to empty.
83	    const before: Record<string, EntityState> = prev.children?.[type] ?? {}
84	    const after: Record<string, EntityState> = next.children?.[type] ?? {}
85	
86	    for (const [id, state] of Object.entries(after)) {
87	      if (!before[id]) {
88	        drafts.push({
89	          action: attach ? "attached" : "created",
90	          entity_type: type,
91	          entity_id: id,
92	          entity_label: state.label,
93	          changes: [],
94	        })
95	        continue
96	      }
97	
98	      const changes = diffFields(before[id].fields, state.fields)
99	      if (changes.length) {
100	        drafts.push({
101	          action: "updated",
102	          entity_type: type,
103	          entity_id: id,
104	          entity_label: state.label,
105	          changes,
106	        })
107	      }
108	    }
109	
110	    for (const [id, state] of Object.entries(before)) {
111	      if (!after[id]) {
112	        drafts.push({
113	          action: attach ? "detached" : "deleted",
114	          entity_type: type,
115	          entity_id: id,
116	          entity_label: state.label,
117	          changes: [],
118	        })
119	      }
120	    }
121	  }
122	
123	  return drafts
124	}
125
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
78	  fields: Record<string, unknown>
79	}

83	 * that exist on their own, so their appearance is reported as "attached"
84	 * instead of "created".

86	export const CHILD_ENTITY_TYPES = [
87	  { type: "variant", attach: false },
88	  { type: "option", attach: false },
89	  { type: "image", attach: false },
90	  { type: "category", attach: true },
91	  { type: "tag", attach: true },
92	  { type: "sales_channel", attach: true },
93	] as const

95	export type ChildEntityType = (typeof CHILD_ENTITY_TYPES)[number]["type"]
96	
97	export type ProductSnapshot = {
98	  product: EntityState
99	  children: Record<ChildEntityType, Record<string, EntityState>>
100	}
101	
102	/**
103	 * Normalizes a value so equal values compare equal: undefined becomes null,
104	 * dates become ISO strings and BigNumber-like objects become numbers.
105	 */
106	function normalize(value: unknown): unknown {
107	  if (value === undefined) {
108	    return null
109	  }
110	  if (value instanceof Date) {
111	    return value.toISOString()
112	  }
113	  if (
114	    value &&
115	    typeof value === "object" &&
116	    !Array.isArray(value) &&
117	    "value" in (value as object) &&
118	    Object.keys(value as object).every((k) =>
119	      ["value", "precision"].includes(k)
120	    )
121	  ) {
122	    return Number((value as { value: unknown }).value)
123	  }
124	  return value
125	}
126	
127	function pick(source: Record<string, any>, keys: string[]) {
128	  const fields: Record<string, unknown> = {}
129	  for (const key of keys) {
130	    fields[key] = normalize(source[key])
131	  }
132	  return fields
133	}
134	
135	// Last path segment of an image URL, which is readable enough as a label.
136	function fileName(url: string | null | undefined) {
137	  if (!url) {
138	    return null
139	  }
140	  const clean = url.split("?")[0]
141	  return clean.substring(clean.lastIndexOf("/") + 1) || url
142	}
143	
144	function toMap<T extends Record<string, any>>(
145	  items: T[] | null | undefined,
146	  build: (item: T) => EntityState
147	) {
148	  const map: Record<string, EntityState> = {}
149	  for (const item of items ?? []) {
150	    if (item?.id) {
151	      map[item.id] = build(item)
152	    }
153	  }
154	  return map
155	}
156	
157	function variantState(variant: Record<string, any>): EntityState {
158	  const fields = pick(variant, VARIANT_SCALAR_FIELDS)
159	
160	  // One field per option, keyed by option title, so a change reads as
161	  // "option Size: S -> M".
162	  for (const o of variant.options ?? []) {
163	    const title = o?.option?.title
164	    if (title) {
165	      fields[`option ${title}`] = normalize(o.value)
166	    }
167	  }
168	
169	  // One field per price. Prices with rules (for example a region) get the
170	  // rules in the key so they do not collide with the base price.
171	  for (const price of variant.prices ?? []) {
172	    const rules = (price.price_rules ?? [])
173	      .map((r: any) => `${r.attribute}=${r.value}`)
174	      .sort()
175	      .join(",")
176	    const key = `price ${price.currency_code}${rules ? ` (${rules})` : ""}`
177	    fields[key] = normalize(price.amount)
178	  }
179	
180	  return { label: variant.title || variant.sku || null, fields }
181	}
182	
183	export function buildProductSnapshot(
184	  product: Record<string, any>
185	): ProductSnapshot {
186	  return {
187	    product: {
188	      label: product.title ?? null,
189	      fields: pick(product, PRODUCT_SCALAR_FIELDS),
190	    },
191	    children: {
192	      variant: toMap(product.variants, variantState),
193	      option: toMap(product.options, (o) => ({
194	        label: o.title ?? null,
195	        fields: {
196	          title: normalize(o.title),
197	          values: (o.values ?? []).map((v: any) => v.value).sort(),
198	        },
199	      })),
200	      image: toMap(product.images, (i) => ({
201	        label: fileName(i.url),
202	        fields: { url: normalize(i.url) },
203	      })),
204	      category: toMap(product.categories, (c) => ({
205	        label: c.name ?? null,
206	        fields: {},
207	      })),
208	      tag: toMap(product.tags, (t) => ({ label: t.value ?? null, fields: {} })),
209	      sales_channel: toMap(product.sales_channels, (s) => ({
210	        label: s.name ?? null,
211	        fields: {},
212	      })),
213	    },
214	  }
215	}
```

```typescript
import { diffSnapshots } from "../diff-snapshots"
import { buildProductSnapshot } from "../snapshot"

// Tests added for the D6 mutation-testing deliverable (issue 112). The first
// mutation run showed that most surviving mutants were in snapshot.ts: nothing
// checked the individual scalar fields that get compared, and the Date and
// BigNumber branches of normalize() never ran at all. These tests close both
// gaps.

// A product with only the bare minimum. Every scalar field below is missing
// from it, so setting one makes it go from "absent" (null) to a value.
const bareProduct = () => ({
  id: "prod_1",
  title: "Shirt",
  variants: [{ id: "variant_1", title: "Small" }] as any[],
})

// One [field, value] pair per scalar field that snapshot.ts compares. The
// values are chosen so each is different from null and from the others, and so
// that numbers, booleans and strings are all represented.
const PRODUCT_SCALARS: [string, unknown][] = [
  ["title", "New title"],
  ["subtitle", "sub"],
  ["description", "desc"],
  ["handle", "new-handle"],
  ["status", "published"],
  ["thumbnail", "https://cdn.test/t.png"],
  ["discountable", false],
  ["is_giftcard", true],
  ["material", "cotton"],
  ["weight", 5],
  ["length", 6],
  ["height", 7],
  ["width", 8],
  ["origin_country", "us"],
  ["hs_code", "hs1"],
  ["mid_code", "mid1"],
  ["type_id", "ptyp_1"],
  ["collection_id", "pcol_1"],
  ["external_id", "ext_1"],
  ["metadata", { k: "v" }],
]

const VARIANT_SCALARS: [string, unknown][] = [
  ["title", "Large"],
  ["sku", "SKU-1"],
  ["barcode", "bar"],
  ["ean", "ean1"],
  ["upc", "upc1"],
  ["allow_backorder", true],
  ["manage_inventory", true],
  ["hs_code", "hs2"],
  ["origin_country", "ca"],
  ["mid_code", "mid2"],
  ["material", "wool"],
  ["weight", 1],
  ["length", 2],
  ["height", 3],
  ["width", 4],
]

describe("buildProductSnapshot scalar fields", () => {
  // If a field name were dropped or blanked in snapshot.ts, a change to that
  // field would produce no activity entry, so the diff would be empty.
  it.each(PRODUCT_SCALARS)(
    "records a change to product %s",
    (field, value) => {
      const next: any = bareProduct()
      next[field] = value

      const entries = diffSnapshots(
        buildProductSnapshot(bareProduct()),
        buildProductSnapshot(next),
        "prod_1"
      )

      expect(entries).toHaveLength(1)
      expect(entries[0]).toMatchObject({
        action: "updated",
        entity_type: "product",
      })
      // `title` is set on both sides, so its "from" is the old title.
      const from = field === "title" ? "Shirt" : null
      expect(entries[0].changes).toEqual([{ field, from, to: value }])
    }
  )

  it.each(VARIANT_SCALARS)(
    "records a change to variant %s",
    (field, value) => {
      const next: any = bareProduct()
      next.variants[0][field] = value

      const entries = diffSnapshots(
        buildProductSnapshot(bareProduct()),
        buildProductSnapshot(next),
        "prod_1"
      )

      expect(entries).toHaveLength(1)
      expect(entries[0]).toMatchObject({
        action: "updated",
        entity_type: "variant",
        entity_id: "variant_1",
      })
      const from = field === "title" ? "Small" : null
      expect(entries[0].changes).toEqual([{ field, from, to: value }])
    }
  )
})

describe("buildProductSnapshot value normalization", () => {
  const fieldsOf = (extra: Record<string, unknown>) =>
    buildProductSnapshot({ ...bareProduct(), ...extra }).product.fields

  it("turns a Date into an ISO string", () => {
    const fields = fieldsOf({ material: new Date("2026-03-04T05:06:07.000Z") })

    expect(fields.material).toBe("2026-03-04T05:06:07.000Z")
  })

  it("turns a BigNumber-like { value, precision } object into a number", () => {
    // The shape the Query graph returns for BigNumber columns such as weight.
    expect(fieldsOf({ weight: { value: "12.5", precision: 20 } }).weight).toBe(
      12.5
    )
    // `precision` is optional; an object with only `value` is converted too.
    expect(fieldsOf({ weight: { value: "3" } }).weight).toBe(3)
  })

  it("does not treat other objects as BigNumbers", () => {
    // Extra keys mean this is real data (metadata), not a BigNumber, so it
    // must come back unchanged rather than collapse to a number.
    const metadata = { value: 1, label: "keep me" }
    expect(fieldsOf({ metadata }).metadata).toEqual(metadata)

    // Arrays and plain nulls are left alone as well.
    expect(fieldsOf({ metadata: [1, 2] }).metadata).toEqual([1, 2])
    expect(fieldsOf({ metadata: null }).metadata).toBeNull()
  })

  it("maps undefined to null", () => {
    expect(fieldsOf({}).subtitle).toBeNull()
  })

  it("treats a BigNumber price and the same plain number as equal", () => {
    const withPrice = (amount: unknown) => ({
      ...bareProduct(),
      variants: [
        {
          id: "variant_1",
          title: "Small",
          prices: [{ currency_code: "usd", amount, price_rules: [] }],
        },
      ],
    })

    const prev = buildProductSnapshot(withPrice(10))

    // Same amount in BigNumber form: not a change.
    expect(
      diffSnapshots(
        prev,
        buildProductSnapshot(withPrice({ value: "10", precision: 20 })),
        "prod_1"
      )
    ).toEqual([])

    // A different BigNumber amount is reported as a plain number.
    const [entry] = diffSnapshots(
      prev,
      buildProductSnapshot(withPrice({ value: "12", precision: 20 })),
      "prod_1"
    )
    expect(entry.changes).toEqual([{ field: "price usd", from: 10, to: 12 }])
  })
})
```

```text
172	/**
173	 * Works out which inventory items the bundle variant must be linked to.
174	 *
175	 * For each component, its variant's inventory links are copied with
176	 * `required_quantity = component quantity * the link's own required_quantity`.
177	 * If two components share an inventory item, the amounts are added together.
178	 *
179	 * Example: 2x lens (lens uses 1 item "L") + 1x kit (uses 3 of "L")
180	 * gives one link "L" with required_quantity 5.
181	 */
182	export function buildBundleInventoryLinks(
183	  components: BundleComponentInput[],
184	  variants: BundleComponentVariant[]
185	): BundleInventoryLink[] {
186	  const variantsById = new Map(variants.map((variant) => [variant.id, variant]))
187	  const merged = new Map<string, number>()
188	
189	  for (const component of components) {
190	    const variant = variantsById.get(component.variant_id)
191	
192	    for (const link of variant?.inventory_items ?? []) {
193	      merged.set(
194	        link.inventory_item_id,

196	          component.quantity * link.required_quantity
197	      )

199	  }

201	  return [...merged.entries()].map(([inventory_item_id, required_quantity]) => ({
202	    inventory_item_id,
203	    required_quantity,
204	  }))
205	}

278	    metadata === null ||
279	    (typeof metadata === "object" &&
280	      metadata !== undefined &&
281	      Object.keys(metadata as object).length === 0)
282	  )
283	}
284	
285	/**
286	 * Makes a plain product update safe for an existing bundle.
287	 *
288	 * - A `null` or `{}` metadata value is dropped, so it doesn't erase the bundle
289	 *   marker. (Other keys are still merged by the base service, and a key can be
290	 *   removed by setting it to an empty string, as for any product.)
291	 * - Variants without an `id` would create a second variant, so the update is
292	 *   rejected.
293	 *
294	 * Returns a copy; the input is not modified.
295	 *
296	 * @param update - one product's update data
297	 * @param bundle - the existing bundle the update targets
298	 */
299	export function protectBundleUpdate<T extends Record<string, any>>(
300	  update: T,
301	  bundle: { id: string; title?: string | null }
302	): T {
303	  const variants = update.variants as { id?: string }[] | null | undefined
304	
305	  if (variants?.some((variant) => !variant.id)) {
306	    throw new MedusaError(
307	      MedusaError.Types.NOT_ALLOWED,
308	      `A variant can't be added to the bundle "${bundle.title}" (${bundle.id}). A bundle has exactly one variant.`
309	    )
310	  }
311	
312	  // `mergeMetadata` deletes a key whose value is "" (and a null value would
313	  // overwrite it), so naming the marker key with an empty value removes it.
314	  // The HTTP validator already blocks the key, this protects direct workflow
315	  // calls too. Setting real components is how the bundle workflows write it.
316	  const metadata = update.metadata as Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined
317	  if (
318	    metadata &&
319	    typeof metadata === "object" &&
320	    BUNDLE_METADATA_KEY in metadata &&
321	    (metadata[BUNDLE_METADATA_KEY] === "" ||
322	      metadata[BUNDLE_METADATA_KEY] === null ||
323	      metadata[BUNDLE_METADATA_KEY] === undefined)
324	  ) {
325	    throw new MedusaError(
326	      MedusaError.Types.NOT_ALLOWED,
327	      `The bundle marker of "${bundle.title}" (${bundle.id}) can't be removed. Delete the bundle instead.`
328	    )
329	  }
330	
331	  if (update.metadata !== undefined && isEmptyMetadataUpdate(update.metadata)) {
332	    const { metadata: _dropped, ...rest } = update
333	    return rest as T
334	  }
335	
336	  return update
337	}
338	
339	/**
340	 * Throws when creating variants would give a bundle more than one variant.
341	 * Creating a bundle itself is allowed: its product has no variants yet when its
342	 * single variant is created.
343	 *
344	 * @param products - the products the variants are created for (with their
345	 *   current variant count)
346	 * @param newVariantsByProduct - how many variants the request adds per product
347	 */
348	export function assertBundleKeepsSingleVariant(
349	  products: {
350	    id: string
351	    title?: string | null
352	    metadata?: Record<string, unknown> | null
353	    variantCount: number
354	  }[],
355	  newVariantsByProduct: Record<string, number>
356	): void {
357	  for (const product of products) {
358	    if (!isBundleMetadata(product.metadata)) {
359	      continue
360	    }
361	
362	    if (product.variantCount + (newVariantsByProduct[product.id] ?? 0) > 1) {
363	      throw new MedusaError(
364	        MedusaError.Types.NOT_ALLOWED,
365	        `A variant can't be added to the bundle "${product.title}" (${product.id}). A bundle has exactly one variant.`
366	      )
367	    }
368	  }
369	}
370	
371	/**
372	 * Throws when any of the variants belongs to a bundle. Deleting a bundle's
373	 * variant would leave a bundle without a variant; delete the bundle instead.
374	 */
375	export function assertNoBundleVariants(
376	  variants: {
377	    id: string
378	    product?: {
379	      id: string
380	      title?: string | null
381	      metadata?: Record<string, unknown> | null
382	    } | null
383	  }[]
384	): void {
385	  const bundles = new Map<string, string | null | undefined>()
386	
387	  for (const variant of variants) {
388	    if (variant.product && isBundleMetadata(variant.product.metadata)) {
389	      bundles.set(variant.product.id, variant.product.title)
390	    }
391	  }
392	
393	  if (bundles.size) {
394	    throw new MedusaError(
395	      MedusaError.Types.NOT_ALLOWED,
396	      `A variant of a bundle can't be deleted: ${[...bundles.entries()]
397	        .map(([id, title]) => `"${title}" (${id})`)
398	        .join(", ")}. Delete the bundle instead.`
399	    )
400	  }
401	}
402	
403	/**
404	 * Returns the id of a bundle's one variant. Throws if the bundle doesn't have
405	 * exactly one, instead of silently picking the wrong variant.
406	 */
407	export function getBundleVariantId(product: {
408	  id: string
409	  variants?: { id: string }[] | null
410	}): string {
411	  if (product.variants?.length !== 1) {
412	    throw new MedusaError(
413	      MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
414	      `Bundle ${product.id} has ${
415	        product.variants?.length ?? 0
416	      } variants but must have exactly 1.`
417	    )
418	  }
```

```typescript
import { MedusaError } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import {
  assertNoBundleUsesVariants,
  assertNoBundleVariants,
  buildBundleInventoryLinks,
  getBundleVariantId,
  isEmptyMetadataUpdate,
  protectBundleUpdate,
  validateBundleComponents,
} from "../bundle"

// Tests added for the D6 mutation-testing deliverable (issue #112).
//
// The first Stryker run on bundle.ts scored 90.15%. Of the 20 mutants that were
// not killed, 14 were real test gaps: error messages that were never checked
// beyond their type (so blanking the ", " list separator went unnoticed) and
// a few input edge cases (missing optional fields, non-object metadata).
// Each test below names the mutants (by line in bundle.ts) that it kills.

// Runs `fn` and returns the error it throws (or undefined if it doesn't), so
// a test can check the error type and the full message.
function thrown(fn: () => unknown): any {
  try {
    fn()
  } catch (e) {
    return e
  }
  return undefined
}

// A variant that is a valid bundle component.
const validVariant = (id: string) => ({
  id,
  manage_inventory: true,
  inventory_items: [{ inventory_item_id: `inv_${id}`, required_quantity: 1 }],
})

// Product metadata that marks a product as a bundle containing `variantId`.
const bundleMetadata = (variantId: string) => ({
  bundle: { components: [{ variant_id: variantId, quantity: 1 }] },
})

describe("validateBundleComponents error messages", () => {
  // Kills the StringLiteral mutant on line 120: the ", " separator between
  // the repeated variants. One duplicate never shows the separator, so two
  // different duplicates are needed.
  it("lists every duplicated variant, separated by commas", () => {
    const error = thrown(() =>
      validateBundleComponents(
        [
          { variant_id: "a", quantity: 1 },
          { variant_id: "a", quantity: 1 },
          { variant_id: "b", quantity: 1 },
          { variant_id: "b", quantity: 1 },
        ],
        []
      )
    )

    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(MedusaError)
    expect(error.message).toContain("listed more than once: a, b.")
  })

  // Kills the ArrowFunction mutant on line 133 (the map that picks the variant
  // id) and the StringLiteral mutant on line 134 (the separator).
  it("names every variant with an invalid quantity", () => {
    const error = thrown(() =>
      validateBundleComponents(
        [
          { variant_id: "a", quantity: 0 },
          { variant_id: "b", quantity: 1.5 },
        ],
        [validVariant("a"), validVariant("b")]
      )
    )

    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(MedusaError)
    expect(error.message).toContain("Invalid for variants: a, b.")
  })

  // Kills the StringLiteral mutant on line 146 (separator of missing variants).
  it("names every variant that was not found", () => {
    const error = thrown(() =>
      validateBundleComponents(
        [
          { variant_id: "a", quantity: 1 },
          { variant_id: "b", quantity: 1 },
        ],
        []
      )
    )

    expect(error.type).toBe(MedusaError.Types.NOT_FOUND)
    expect(error.message).toContain("were not found: a, b.")
  })
})

describe("validateBundleComponents optional fields", () => {
  const components = [
    { variant_id: "a", quantity: 1 },
    { variant_id: "b", quantity: 1 },
  ]

  // Kills the OptionalChaining mutant on line 155. A variant that has no
  // inventory_items at all must be rejected with a MedusaError, not crash with
  // a TypeError when `.length` is read from undefined.
  it("rejects a variant with no inventory items as a normal error", () => {
    const error = thrown(() =>
      validateBundleComponents(components, [
        validVariant("a"),
        { id: "b", manage_inventory: true },
      ])
    )

    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(MedusaError)
    expect(error.type).toBe(MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA)
    expect(error.message).toContain("doesn't track inventory")
  })

  // Kills the OptionalChaining mutant on line 163. A loaded variant without a
  // `product` is still a valid component; reading `.metadata` of undefined must
  // not throw.
  it("accepts variants that were loaded without their product", () => {
    expect(
      thrown(() =>
        validateBundleComponents(components, [
          validVariant("a"),
          validVariant("b"),
        ])
      )
    ).toBeUndefined()
  })
})

describe("buildBundleInventoryLinks missing data", () => {
  // Kills the OptionalChaining mutant on line 192 (`variant?.`): a component
  // whose variant was not loaded contributes no links instead of crashing.
  it("skips a component whose variant was not loaded", () => {
    const links = buildBundleInventoryLinks(
      [
        { variant_id: "missing", quantity: 1 },
        { variant_id: "a", quantity: 2 },
      ],
      [validVariant("a")]
    )

    expect(links).toEqual([{ inventory_item_id: "inv_a", required_quantity: 2 }])
  })

  // Kills the NoCoverage ArrayDeclaration mutant on line 192 (the `?? []`
  // fallback was never reached): a variant with no inventory_items gives no
  // links.
  it("gives no links for a variant without inventory items", () => {
    expect(
      buildBundleInventoryLinks(
        [{ variant_id: "a", quantity: 1 }],
        [{ id: "a", manage_inventory: true }]
      )
    ).toEqual([])
  })
})

describe("bundle usage and variant errors list every item", () => {
  // Kills the StringLiteral mutant on line 257: the ", " between bundles.
  it("names every bundle that uses the variant", () => {
    const error = thrown(() =>
      assertNoBundleUsesVariants(
        [
          { id: "b1", title: "A", metadata: bundleMetadata("v1") },
          { id: "b2", title: "B", metadata: bundleMetadata("v1") },
        ],

    expect(error.message).toContain(`"A" (b1), "B" (b2)`)
  })

  it("names every bundle whose variant is being deleted", () => {
    const error = thrown(() =>
      assertNoBundleVariants([

          id: "v1",
          product: { id: "p1", title: "A", metadata: bundleMetadata("x") },
        },
        {
          id: "v2",
          product: { id: "p2", title: "B", metadata: bundleMetadata("y") },
        },
      ])
    )

    expect(error.message).toContain(`"A" (p1), "B" (p2)`)
  })
})

describe("isEmptyMetadataUpdate edge cases", () => {
  // Kills the LogicalOperator mutant on line 279 (&& changed to ||): a
  // non-empty object is a real update, not an empty one.
  it("is false for an object with keys", () => {
    expect(isEmptyMetadataUpdate({ a: 1 })).toBe(false)
  })

  // Kills the ConditionalExpression mutant on line 279 (the typeof check
  // forced true): non-object values such as "" and 0 have no keys, so without
  // the typeof check they would wrongly count as empty updates.
  it("is false for non-object values", () => {
    expect(isEmptyMetadataUpdate("")).toBe(false)
    expect(isEmptyMetadataUpdate(0)).toBe(false)
  })
})

describe("protectBundleUpdate marker removal", () => {
  // Kills the ConditionalExpression mutant on line 323. A marker key that is
  // present but explicitly undefined must also be rejected.
  it("rejects an update that sets the bundle marker to undefined", () => {
    const error = thrown(() =>
      protectBundleUpdate(
        { metadata: { bundle: undefined } },
        { id: "prod_1", title: "Bundle" }
      )
    )

    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(MedusaError)
    expect(error.type).toBe(MedusaError.Types.NOT_ALLOWED)
    expect(error.message).toContain("can't be removed")
  })
})

describe("getBundleVariantId error message", () => {
  // Kills the LogicalOperator mutant on line 415 (`?? 0` changed to `&& 0`).
  // With the mutant, a missing variants list prints "undefined" and a list of
  // two prints "0".
  it("reports 0 variants when the list is missing", () => {
    const error = thrown(() => getBundleVariantId({ id: "prod_1" }))

    expect(error.message).toBe("Bundle prod_1 has 0 variants but must have exactly 1.")
  })

  it("reports the real count when there are too many", () => {
    const error = thrown(() =>
      getBundleVariantId({ id: "prod_1", variants: [{ id: "a" }, { id: "b" }] })
    )

    expect(error.message).toBe("Bundle prod_1 has 2 variants but must have exactly 1.")
  })
})
```

```markdown
## Questions

1. **What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?**
   The existing 43 tests checked that the right error type was thrown, but not what the error said. Seven of the 14 gaps were list separators and variant ids inside messages (lines 120, 133, 134, 146, 257, 398, 415). These messages only ever showed a single item in the tests, so a list of several items was untested, even though acceptance criterion 11 says the error must name every bundle. The other 7 were edge cases around absent optional fields (`inventory_items`, `product`, an unloaded variant) and non-object or `undefined` metadata. The suite was good at the main paths and weak at inputs that are valid but unusual. The 6 equivalent mutants are defensive defaults and redundant checks, where no test could tell the difference.

2. **Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the requirements? Explain.**
   No existing assertion had a wrong expected value. The survivors came from assertions that were missing, not from assertions with incorrect values. The reverse is true of the tests I added: the separator tests expect messages such as `"A" (b1), "B" (b2)` and `a, b`. Those exact strings come from how `bundle.ts` formats its messages, not from a requirement. Requirement 11 only demands that every bundle is named, so a different separator would still meet the requirement and would fail these tests. The tests check the "every item is listed" behavior, but they also pin the comma-and-space format, which is stricter than the requirements.

3. **If you used AI to configure the tool, analyze survivors, or write tests, what did it produce and what did you verify or correct?**
   AI (Claude Code) was used for all three. It installed `@stryker-mutator/core` and `@stryker-mutator/jest-runner`, wrote `stryker.config.mjs`, classified the 20 survivors, and wrote `bundle-edge-cases.spec.ts`. What was corrected or checked along the way:
```
